The AR module pilot, Charles Duke, criticized the film's portrayal of Swigert as unprepared for the flight, stating that Swigert was very familiar with the module as he had also long worked on developing it. The dialogue between ground control and the astronauts in the film was taken nearly verbatim from transcripts and recordings, with the exception of the tagline "Houston, we have a problem." The actual words uttered by Swigert were "Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here."

In the film, during the re-entry blackout, Tom Hanks (as Lovell) says "Hello Houston... this is Odyssey... it's good to see you again." However, in the actual re-entry, the Command Module's transmission was not received until after the blackout.

In his book "Apollo 13," Jim Lovell describes his experience during the re-entry blackout: "I felt my body being raised off the floor, and then I was floating, suspended in the air. I could see the people in the room looking up at me, their faces a blurry mass of color."

In Luke 3:23-38, the genealogy of Jesus is traced back to Adam, who is referred to as "the son of God." The Greek text of Luke's Gospel does not use the word "son" in the genealogy after "son of Joseph." The genealogy descends from the Davidic line through Nathan, who is an otherwise little-known son of David.
